8. Composing contracts

Say the billing team owns a step that cleans up orders, and you own the step after it, which doubles the amounts for a promotion. You've never read their code, and you shouldn't have to; but if a negative amount slips past them, your step doubles it and your name is on the incident. What you rely on is their contract. If each step has one, the contracts should compose: when one step's output feeds another, the downstream step's preconditions should follow from what the upstream step guarantees, with no need to check the intermediate data. That is exactly what happens. When the input of a contracted function is the result of another contracted function, sverify:
  1. proves the downstream preconditions from the upstream contract (they are never checked on data), and
  2. proves the downstream postconditions assuming only what the upstream step guarantees, not what its code happens to do.

Two steps that fit together

data.text/html:
postcondition status
(_.doubled >= 0) ✅ proved
_.doubled.notnull() ✅ proved
runtime ⚠️ may wrap around: ($2 * 2)
output column known values
id any integer or NULL
customer a string or NULL
doubled an integer ≥ 0

data.text/markdown:
The requires paid: … rows say what doubled was allowed to assume: the guarantees of paid, not facts about orders. Each link is a Hoare triple, the classic notation of program verification: {P} f {Q} means "if P holds before f, then Q holds after". The rule
{P} g {Q} and {Q} f {S} give {P} f ∘ g {S}
is theorem Triple.compose in SubstraitLean/Compose.lean.

When the link breaks

Now we'll swap the step upstream for one that promises less. Pick what feeds doubled:

<marimo-callout-output data-html='"\u003cspan class=\"markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"paragraph\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCompositionError\u003c/strong\u003e: doubled needs (_.amount &gt;= 0) (it is TRUE or FALSE) on 't'; not_null only guarantees _.amount.notnull()\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-kind='"danger"'></marimo-callout-output>

data.text/markdown:
• not_null guarantees too little: doubled needs amount ≥ 0, and nothing upstream promises it. The error names both sides of the broken link. (not_null's own code would happen to keep negative amounts, but that's beside the point: only the contract counts.)
  • A plain Ibis step carries no contract of its own. What follows from its operations is still proved: amount > 0 implies both of doubled's preconditions. With only amount IS NOT NULL, the missing amount ≥ 0 is treated like a precondition on a base table: checked on the data if there is data, assumed otherwise. That's why that choice goes through here.
  • A precondition can also follow from more than the upstream ensures: it is proved as an extra postcondition of the upstream function, from that function's own preconditions. Keys (sv.unique) propagate the same way.

On real data

With bound tables, only the base tables are checked: paid's preconditions on orders. The intermediate result is never inspected; doubled's preconditions were proved. Here are three orders that meet paid's preconditions, including cy's, with an amount of 0:

Where did a result come from?

When the analyst downstream asks why they can trust a number, you'll want to say what it rests on. sverify.contracts.provenance(expr) shows what a contracted result assumed and what it guarantees: guarantees are its proved postconditions, external the preconditions on base tables that the whole chain rests on.

data.text/html:
guarantees
(_.doubled >= 0)
_.doubled.notnull()
base tableassumed
orders(_.amount >= 0)
ordersunique(id)

data.text/markdown: You can now chain steps written by different teams and have every link proved from their contracts alone. The intermediate data is never checked, a step that promises too little is caught before anything runs, and provenance tells the analyst what a number rests on. Orders keep arriving, though, so composed results also need to be kept up to date. Next up, Incremental views maintains a query from its changes alone; chapter 10 then maintains doubled(paid(orders)) incrementally, and shows how its guarantees keep holding while the data changes.
